virginia-state-capitol.name: Virginia State Capitol
virginia-state-capitol.description: Neoclassical capitol building designed with Thomas Jefferson's input, completed in 1788; still houses the Virginia General Assembly.

main-street-station.name: Main Street Station
main-street-station.description: 1901 French Renaissance Revival railway station with a distinctive clock tower, in Shockoe Bottom; still an active Amtrak stop.

the-jefferson-hotel.name: The Jefferson Hotel
the-jefferson-hotel.description: Opulent 1895 Beaux-Arts hotel designed by Carrère and Hastings, known for its grand staircase and rooftop palm court.

old-city-hall.name: Old City Hall
old-city-hall.description: High Victorian Gothic government building completed in 1894, adjacent to Capitol Square; now used as office space.

carpenter-theatre-dominion-energy-center.name: Carpenter Theatre / Dominion Energy Center
carpenter-theatre-dominion-energy-center.description: 1928 Loew's movie palace restored as the Carpenter Theatre, now the anchor venue of the Dominion Energy Center for the Performing Arts.

federal-reserve-bank-of-richmond.name: Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond
federal-reserve-bank-of-richmond.description: Aluminum-clad Fifth District Federal Reserve headquarters tower designed by Minoru Yamasaki, built 1975-1978 overlooking the James River.

james-monroe-building.name: James Monroe Building
james-monroe-building.description: State office tower on Capitol Square housing several Virginia state agencies, named for President James Monroe.

dominion-energy-tower-600-canal-place.name: Dominion Energy tower (600 Canal Place)
dominion-energy-tower-600-canal-place.description: High-rise corporate headquarters of Dominion Energy at 600 Canal Place, one of the tallest buildings in downtown Richmond's skyline.

altria-theater.name: Altria Theater
altria-theater.description: 1927 Shriners' Mosque-style auditorium later known as the Landmark Theater, now a major performing arts and concert venue near Monroe Park.

byrd-theatre.name: Byrd Theatre
byrd-theatre.description: Lavish 1928 movie palace on Cary Street with an original Wurlitzer organ, still operating as a single-screen cinema.

monument-avenue-streetscape.name: Monument Avenue streetscape
monument-avenue-streetscape.description: Grand tree-lined boulevard of Victorian and Beaux-Arts mansions with a landscaped median, a National Historic Landmark district.

hollywood-cemetery.name: Hollywood Cemetery
hollywood-cemetery.description: 1849 rural garden cemetery on the James River bluffs, burial site of two U.S. presidents and Confederate president Jefferson Davis.

belle-isle-footbridge.name: Belle Isle footbridge
belle-isle-footbridge.description: Pedestrian suspension footbridge beneath the Robert E. Lee Bridge connecting downtown to Belle Isle, a former factory site turned riverfront park.

mayo-bridge.name: Mayo Bridge
mayo-bridge.description: Richmond's oldest James River highway crossing, carrying US 360; the current structure dates to 1913 on a river-crossing site used since colonial times.

canal-walk-tredegar-iron-works.name: Canal Walk + Tredegar Iron Works
canal-walk-tredegar-iron-works.description: Riverfront walkway along the historic James River and Kanawha Canal, passing the ruins of the Tredegar Iron Works, a Confederate munitions foundry now home to the American Civil War Museum.

the-diamond.name: The Diamond
the-diamond.description: 1985 baseball stadium on North Arthur Ashe Boulevard, longtime home of the Richmond Flying Squirrels, now succeeded by a new ballpark under the CarMax Park name.

vcu-cabell-library.name: VCU Cabell Library
vcu-cabell-library.description: Main library of Virginia Commonwealth University's Monroe Park campus, named for novelist James Branch Cabell.

maggie-l-walker-memorial.name: Maggie L. Walker memorial
maggie-l-walker-memorial.description: Bronze statue of banker and civic leader Maggie L. Walker by sculptor Toby Mendez, dedicated 2017 at Broad and Adams streets in Jackson Ward.
